newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat-Higher prices prompt sales.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat-Higher prices prompt sales.

text.p: Higher cash bids prompted increased farmer selling of old- and new-crop wheat across the northern U.S., grain dealers said.
Cash bids to farmers showed smaller gains than those recorded in U.S. wheat futures markets because dealers lowered basis bids.

Minneapolis dealers said flood waters from the Mississippi River and its tributaries receded south of the city. At least one elevator in Savage reopened to accept truck grain, but the river was still too high to load barges.
Montana farmers contracted to sell new-crop hard red winter wheat when prices topped $4.00 per bushel, dealers there said. "We bought 80,000 bushels this morning," said a Billings dealer.
Some dealers in the Pacific Northwest said movement was very limited. "We never bought a kernel of wheat this morning," an Oregon merchandiser said.
